text:
maya: quick ping — PR #17999 is ready (small timeout fix). CI jobs are still queued (mac/linux/gpu matrix). Nightly deploy freeze starts 21:00 UTC. Do we hold for the rebase window at 22:30 or run a canary to dedicated to avoid missing the patch cutoff? need guidance + approval.

sam: :eyes: are tests failing or just waiting in queue?

maya: just queueing; none have run yet. ci-bot says long backlog. also needs one review from @ali (security touchpoint).

ali: I can do a quick review in ~20m. if queue still blocked then i'd rather hold for the rebase window than force-merge.

rachel: if we hold we might miss the patch release cutoff. running a manual canary to dedicated seems low-risk for this change. @ops any blockers for canary?

deploy-bot: production blackout begins 21:00 UTC. canary deploys are allowed but require the "canary-ops" tag and a manual ops approval.

ci-bot: queue position: 84, estimated start ~48m.

maya: plan proposal — @ali please review; if you approve i'll tag canary-ops and kick off a manual canary to the dedicated pool and monitor for 20m. if anything looks off we revert. if CI finishes earlier, we can merge in the rebase window. /cc @sam @rachel

sam: +1 to that plan.

ali: quick review done, left one minor nit. will approve once fixed.

maya: pushed fix and requested merge. will wait for the approval then run this: ```bash
git rebase origin/main && gh pr merge 17999 --merge --body "canary to dedicated"
``` will hold final merge until canary stable for 20m unless CI finishes earlier.

rachel: :thumbsup: keep us posted.

ci-bot: job started on runner-12 at 1765889020 (integration-matrix).

maya: canary started on dedicated, monitoring metrics — latency and error-rate look normal so far. holding for 20m.

maya: canary stable, proceeding with merge to main (no regressions observed).
